# Tobit Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** This is the book of the acts of Tobit son of Tobiel son of Ananiel son of Aduel son of Gabael son of Raphael son of Raguel, from the lineage of Asiel, of the tribe of Naphtali,

**2** who was taken captive in the days of Enemessar king of the Assyrians, from Thisbe, which lies to the south of Kedesh-Naphtali in upper Galilee, above Asher, toward the west, north of Phogor.

**3** I, Tobit, walked in the paths of truth and righteous deeds all the days of my life. I performed many acts of mercy for my kindred and for my people who had gone into exile with me to Nineveh in the land of the Assyrians.

**4** When I was still in my own land, in the land of Israel — while I was yet young — the entire tribe of Naphtali my ancestor defected from the house of Jerusalem, which had been chosen out of all the tribes of Israel for all the tribes to offer sacrifice there, where the temple of the dwelling of the Most High had been consecrated and established for all generations of the age.

**5** All the tribes that had revolted with them were sacrificing to the calf of Baal, as were the house of Jeroboam my forefather.

**6** But I alone would frequently go up to Jerusalem for the appointed feasts, as it is prescribed as an everlasting ordinance for all Israel. I would bring the firstfruits and the tithes of my produce and the firstborn animals and the first shearings of the sheep,

**7** and give them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, at the altar. The tithe of grain, wine, olive oil, pomegranates, figs, and the rest of the fruit I would give to the sons of Levi who ministered at Jerusalem. The second tithe I would convert to silver for six years and then go up to Jerusalem and spend it there each year.

**8** The third tithe I would give to the orphans and widows and to the resident aliens who had attached themselves to the children of Israel. I would bring it and give it every third year, and we would eat it in accordance with the ordinance prescribed in the law of Moses and according to the commands that Deborah the mother of our forefather Ananiel had charged us — for my father had died and left me an orphan.

**9** When I came of age I took a wife from our father's own lineage; her name was Anna, and she bore me a son named Tobias.

**10** After I was taken captive to Assyria and came as a prisoner to Nineveh, all my kindred and countrymen ate from the food of the Gentiles,

**11** but I myself kept strict watch over myself and did not eat,

**12** for I kept God in mind with my whole soul.

**13** The Most High granted me favor and good standing before Enemessar, and I became his purveyor.

**14** I would travel to Media and make purchases for him until his death. During that time I deposited ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael the brother of Gabrias, in the region of Media.

**15** When Enemessar died, his son Sennacherib reigned in his place. The roads through Media became unsafe, and I could no longer make the journey there.

**16** In the days of Enemessar I performed many acts of mercy for my kinspeople:

**17** I gave my bread to the hungry and my clothing to the naked; and whenever I saw any of my kinspeople dead and thrown out on the walls of Nineveh, I would bury them.

**18** When Sennacherib returned, having fled from Judea in the days of the judgment that the King of Heaven brought upon him for the blasphemies he had uttered, and he was killing many of the Israelites — I would bury their bodies in secret. For in his rage he was putting many to death, and I would steal their corpses and bury them; Sennacherib searched for them and could not find them.

**19** Then a certain Ninevite went and informed the king that I was the one burying them. When I learned that I had been denounced to the king and that my life was being sought, I was afraid and fled.

**20** Everything I possessed was confiscated; nothing was left to me but my wife Anna and my son Tobias.

**21** But before forty days had passed, two of his sons murdered him and fled to the mountains of Ararat. His son Sarchedonus reigned in his place and appointed Achiacharus son of my brother Anael over all the financial accounts of his kingdom and over the entire administration.

**22** Achiacharus put in a word for me, and I returned to Nineveh. Achiacharus had been chief cupbearer, keeper of the signet ring, steward, and treasurer; Sarchedonus had made him second in authority. He was my nephew, from my own family.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- "acts of mercy" (eleēmosynas): This is the thematic keyword of Tobit, occurring throughout chapters 1-4. It encompasses almsgiving, charity, and covenant-faithfulness. LOGOS renders consistently as "acts of mercy."
- "of the Most High" (tou hypsistou): Used throughout as an honorific divine title. LOGOS preserves "the Most High" rather than substituting "God" for formal consistency.
- Verse 4: "defected from the house of Jerusalem" — the Greek apostasin literally means "apostasy/departure." The religious dimension is intentional.
- Verse 7: The three-tithe system maps to Num 18 and Deut 14; the narrative establishes Tobit's scrupulous observance before the exile narrative.
- Verse 8: Deborah the grandmother is named only in the GII Sinaiticus text; this is a distinctive feature of the longer recension.
- Verse 18: "King of Heaven" — a Persian-period divine title that dates the book's composition milieu.
- Verse 21: "Sarchedonus" = Esarhaddon (historical king of Assyria, 681–669 BCE); Achiacharus is the protagonist of the Ahiqar wisdom tradition, here incorporated into Tobit's family.

*— LOGOS*
